为智能眼镜设计

智能眼镜以全天佩戴为设计目标，让用户解放双手，便捷地获取信息。设计智能的增强体验，帮助用户更专注于真实世界、更投入当下。借助设计指南与 UI 套件，将应用体验延伸到无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜。

为用户带来增强体验

智能眼镜让 Android 应用进入一种全新、与个人高度贴近的设备形态。为无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜设计的应用，应丰富日常生活，提供无需动手的实用功能，让用户能在不引人注意的情况下使用数字服务。

认识两种眼镜形态

无屏眼镜

带屏眼镜

有了显示屏，可以让声音与轻量、一眼可读的视觉信息相互配合。高对比、精简的画面用于呈现导航或通知等内容，只在相关时出现，为视野补充信息，避免遮挡。你可以为带屏眼镜构建应用，并设计适合显示屏的专属交互。

title: 设计原则
description: 让眼镜自然融入日常生活，以舒适、一眼可读和恰到好处的交互为出发点。
body:
为搭载 Android XR 的智能眼镜设计应用，需要认真考虑用户体验，把使用舒适和融入日常生活放在首位。眼镜上的应用应像用户感知能力的自然延伸，让人方便地获取信息，又不造成打扰。

无屏眼镜与带屏眼镜

无屏眼镜轻巧便携，适合全天佩戴。借助内置扬声器、摄像头和麦克风，设计师与开发者可以打造无需动手、能够辅助现实活动的智能体验。

带屏眼镜在此基础上增加了一块小型显示屏，让用户在私人视野中看到更多信息，并与声音输出相互配合。

设计这类增强体验时，应同时考虑无屏和带屏两种眼镜形态。

以多模态交互为先

界面应适应语音、手势等能够解放双手的交互方式。设计交互时，要充分考虑间接控制，以及部分输入方式精度有限所带来的约束。

一眼可读，按需出现

带屏眼镜上的交互通常很短暂。界面应便于扫一眼就理解，元素也应短暂呈现。

只在需要时显示界面，任务完成后及时退去，尽量减少一直停留在视野中的干扰。

透明界面始终与真实世界争夺注意力

眼镜的显示视野有限，对焦距离可能变化，现实背景也可能持续变化。信息呈现应简洁，并能适应这些变化。

优化文字排版，让内容清晰易读，避免过多信息给用户造成负担。

让用户专注于关键内容

布局应突出必要信息，减少操作项和视觉元素，帮助用户保持专注。

根据有限的显示视野控制内容密度，避免认知过载，让阅读更舒适。

以舒适为先

用户的舒适感最重要。避免过多视觉信息或声音提醒造成负担。优先采用清晰、简洁的表达与交互，避免分散用户对现实活动的注意力，尤其是在用户正在移动，或需要全神贯注地留意周围环境时。眼镜独特的形态与硬件能力，需要专门的设计考量。

  • 清楚说明收集哪些数据、为什么收集，以及如何存储。
  • 避免突兀、分散注意力的视觉通知，以免在关键时刻遮挡用户视线。
  • 如果应用有声音输出，音量不应盖过环境声。用户必须始终能够感知周围环境。
  • 避免可能引发晕动不适的界面和动效，例如要求用户边走路边阅读大量文字。
  • 遵循 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 的界面最佳实践，兼顾各种可能环境下的阅读体验与清晰可辨性。
bodyEn:
Designing for intelligent eyewear with Android XR requires a thoughtful approach to user experience, prioritizing comfort and seamless integration with the user's daily life. Apps on glasses should feel like a natural extension of the user's perception, providing convenient access to information without being intrusive.

Audio glasses and display glasses

Audio glasses are lightweight and portable for all day wear. With built-in speakers, a camera, and microphone; designers and developers are able to build intelligent and hands-free augmented experiences.

Display glasses provide the addition of a small display, giving users a private screen for seeing additional information, harmonizing with audio output.

Design your augmented experience to take into account both types of glasses with both displayless and display capabilities.

Glasses prioritize multi-modal interactions

Design the user interface for hands-free modalities such as voice or gesture. Carefully consider the limitations of indirect control and less-precise input when designing interactions.

Prioritize glanceable, transient elements

Craft user interfaces with an emphasis on glanceable views and temporary elements, acknowledging the transient nature of interactions on display glasses.

Design UI to appear only when needed and recede when the task is complete, minimizing persistent on-screen distractions.

Transparent UI always competes with the real-world

Present information concisely and adaptively, considering the glasses' small field of view, varying focal distances, and potentially dynamic backgrounds.

Optimize typography for legibility to prevent overwhelming the user with information.

Optimize for focus

Design layouts that prioritize essential information, reducing the number of actions and visual elements to maintain user focus.

Thoughtfully manage content density to respect the limited field of view and prevent cognitive overload for comfortable readability.

Comfort

User comfort is paramount. Avoid overwhelming the user with excessive visual information or audio alerts. Prioritize clear, concise communication and interactions that don't distract from real-world activities, especially when the user is in motion or requires full attention to their surroundings. This unique form factor and its hardware features come with specialized considerations.

  • Be transparent about what data you collect, why you collect it, and how it is stored.
  • Avoid sudden, distracting visual notifications that could obstruct the user's view at critical moments.
  • If your app provides audio, the volume shouldn't block out environmental sounds. Users must remain aware of their surroundings.
  • Avoid UI and motion that could induce motion sickness, such as expecting users to read large amounts of text while walking.
  • Account for reading and legibility in a spectrum of possible environments by following Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI best practices.

title: 专为带屏眼镜打造的界面
description: 认识 Glimmer 如何围绕光学透视显示、硬件输入和使用舒适度构建界面。
body:
使用 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 界面框架，为带屏眼镜打造适用于光学透视显示的增强体验。Glimmer 是最早一批专门针对透明显示和眼镜形态优化的界面框架之一。

从透明显示出发

以研究成果和色彩科学为依据，围绕透明显示与眼镜形态进行优化，让光学透视界面兼顾使用体验与视觉美感。

围绕硬件能力设计输入

交互输入方式围绕带屏眼镜的硬件能力设计。

专为这种设备形态打造

样式和组件均为带屏眼镜及其他光学透视显示设备专门设计，可以直接使用。

Jetpack Compose Glimmer 针对透明显示和用户舒适度做了优化，同时保留定制空间。除了文字样式和颜色，你还可以自定义焦点高亮，掌握应用的视觉表达，并定义符合品牌风格的 GlimmerTheme。

开始设计眼镜体验前，可进一步阅读视觉样式和组件，或直接了解如何开发增强体验。

提示：可以从 Figma 中的 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 设计套件开始。
bodyEn:
Build your UI for display glasses using the Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI framework for augmented experiences that work on optical see-through displays. Jetpack Compose Glimmer is one of the first UI frameworks to be optimized for transparent displays and the glasses form-factor.

Transparent display first

Optimized, and backed by research and color science, for transparent displays and the glasses form factor for thoughtful, beautiful, optical see-through experiences.

Hardware input

Interaction inputs are designed around the capabilities of display glasses.

Purpose-built

Styles and components are purpose-built to use out-of-the-box for display glasses and other devices with optical see-through displays.

Jetpack Compose Glimmer is optimized for transparent displays and user comfort. While purpose built, it's not rigid. It provides a way for you to customize the focus highlights, in addition to type and color. This gives you control over your app's aesthetic, so you can define the GlimmerTheme that fits your brand.

To start designing your glasses experience, read more in the Styles and Components or get started building your augmented experience.

Note: You can start with the Jetpack Compose Glimmer Designkit for Figma.

title: 开始设计
description: 从关键任务出发，依次梳理视觉、声音、输入、系统界面与异常状态。
body:
使用 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 界面框架，打造适用于光学透视显示的增强体验。Glimmer 是最早一批专门针对透明显示和眼镜形态优化的界面框架之一。

1. 选择关键用户旅程

优先选择符合眼镜“一眼可读”原则的关键用户旅程（CUJ）。这类体验可以通过极简界面或纯声音呈现，同时让用户继续关注周围环境。可以从现有应用的使用入口入手，寻找适合延伸到眼镜上的场景。

例如，无需手动操作、逐步提供转向提示的步行导航，可以帮助用户到达目的地。

所选旅程也应考虑安全、舒适和性能原则。例如，避免选择会无必要地长时间占用摄像头，或侵犯用户隐私的任务。

进一步了解基础设计原则。

推荐

从手机应用中提取能发挥眼镜优势的功能，例如一眼可读的体验。

避免

把整个手机应用照搬到眼镜上。手机应用的完整形态并不适合眼镜。

2. 精简体验，适配界面

设计带屏模式的界面时，从主应用的一条关键用户旅程开始：

  • 突出重点：布局优先呈现必要信息，减少操作项和视觉元素，让用户保持专注。
  • 通过纵深表达层级：用深度区分元素的重要程度。
  • 自下而上布局：绘制界面时，从画布底部开始，向上排列组件。
  • 转换视觉组件：为带屏眼镜采用 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 组件和布局模式。

进一步阅读组件与应用界面。

3. 设计声音流程与反馈

让声音交互具有自然的对话感。即使在带屏眼镜上，声音也应承担应用体验中的重要部分；对于无屏眼镜，则需要完整考虑纯声音体验。可以绘制纯声音流程图，用声音提示和对话标注每一步交互及反馈。评估整个流程，避免声音信息过多，给用户造成负担。

4. 明确输入与操作的对应关系

梳理设备控件、手势与应用操作的映射。可以从基本交互开始，例如把应用中的轻点操作映射为触控板轻点。

继续阅读输入方式。

5. 将系统界面纳入设计

设计时也要考虑应用与其他系统界面的关系。

应用会出现在主界面中，也可能通过通知等系统功能呈现；这些内容可能出现在系统栏中。

进一步了解系统界面。

6. 补齐其他状态

应用在无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜上都会遇到不同情况，例如连接异常或权限问题。手机主应用和眼镜应用都应考虑这些状态。

务必为所需的设备功能申请权限。

这些状态需要同时从视觉界面和声音两个方面设计。例如，用语音告知用户需要回到手机完成授权，或读出错误信息。

提示：可使用 Figma 上的 Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI 套件开始设计。
bodyEn:
Build your app using the Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI framework for augmented experiences that work on optical see-through displays. Jetpack Compose Glimmer is one of the first UI frameworks to be optimized for transparent displays and the glasses form-factor.

1. Decide on user journeys

Focus on critical user journeys (CUJs) that are compatible with the glasses form factor's glanceable principles. That could be expressed with minimal UI or audio only while allowing the user to stay present in their surroundings. To find opportunities, consider starting entry points in your current app that would benefit from Glasses.

For example, a user may benefit with hands-free, turn-by-turn walking directions to help them navigate to their destination.

The chosen user journey should also account for safety, comfort, and performance principles. For example, don't choose tasks that would require the user's camera for unnecessarily long periods or infringe on their privacy.

Learn about foundational principles.

Do

Extract features from your mobile app that benefit from the glasses form factor. For example, glanceable experiences.

Don't

Port your entire phone app to glasses as they do not scale to the glasses form factor.

2. Minimize & Translate

For display mode UI, start with a CUJ from your core app:

  • Optimize layouts for focus: Layouts prioritize essential information, reducing the number of actions and visual elements to maintain user focus.

  • Use depth for hierarchy: Depth is used to communicate element priority.

  • Design from the bottom up: When building mocks, start from the bottom, laying out components upward.

  • Translate visual components: For display glasses, use Jetpack Compose Glimmer components and layout patterns.

Read more on components and app view.

3. Audio flow & cues

Get conversational with the audio. While audio should make up a large part of your app's experience even on display glasses, you also need to account for an audio-only experience for audio glasses. You can do this by creating an audio-only flow map to describe this experience. Notate interactions and feedback with audio cues and dialogue. Evaluate your design to avoid overwhelming the user with your audio flow.

4. Map input controls

Make sure to map out the inputs for the device controls and gestures. You can start by translating basic app interactions, like tap, to a trackpad tap.

Continue to inputs.

5. Consider SysUI

Account for other system interfaces.

Your app will appear in the home and other system features, like notifications if used. These can appear in the system bar.

More on System UI

6. Additional states

Your app will encounter different scenarios on audio and display glasses, such as connection or permission issues. Account for these different states both within your core app and glasses app.

Make sure to ask for device feature permissions.

Remember, you will need to consider these through visual UI and audio. For example, give audio feedback to communicate that they should complete a permission flow on their mobile device or to read out errors.

Note: Get started with the Jetpack Compose Glimmer UI Kit on Figma.

title: 界面呈现概览
description: 理解主界面、应用界面和系统栏各自的职责，以及它们与手机之间的衔接。
body:
为带屏眼镜设计界面，需要考虑不同的界面呈现形式和使用情境：眼镜的系统界面（主界面与通知）、投射到眼镜上的应用，以及手机应用中与眼镜顺畅衔接的体验。

这些界面可分为三种形态：主界面、应用界面和系统栏。

主界面

主界面借鉴手机锁屏，是用户熟悉的起点。它只提供少量与当前情境相关的信息和操作。

应用界面

应用界面是呈现应用内容的画布。系统栏默认留空，以便系统提醒出现时尽量少干扰用户视线。

系统栏

系统栏的元素只在需要时短暂出现，例如 Gemini、通知、系统提醒和设备控制。

定制系统界面

系统相关界面的定制空间有限。系统界面采用模板化 API，以保持视觉一致、减少用户在现实环境中受到的打扰，并简化开发。通知扩展内容必须遵循系统定义的模板，只允许少量品牌点缀，以维持一致性。

可以通过系统中的图标颜色表达品牌。
bodyEn:
When designing UI for display glasses, it's crucial to consider various surfaces and contexts. These include the Glasses System UI (Home and Notifications), your app projected on Glasses, and the seamless handoff experience integrated within your mobile application.

Design surfaces can be described in three states: Home, App view, and system bar.

Home

Inspired by the phone's lock screen, home acts as a familiar base for your user. It provides minimal, contextual information and actions.

App view

The app view is the canvas for your app's UI. The system bar is empty by default to allow for system alerts to be less intrusive for the user's line of sight.

System bar

System bar elements temporarily display as needed. This can include Gemini, Notifications, system alerts, device controls, etc.

Customize system surfaces

Customization is limited for interface surfaces, while system UI utilizes templated APIs for a visually cohesive and unobtrusive user experience in real-world settings and effortless developer experience. Content on notification extensions must follow system-defined templates, allowing only minimal brand accents for consistency.

System icons are a color branding opportunity.

title: 系统界面
description: 了解主界面、系统栏、通知与指示灯如何共同构成完整的眼镜体验。
body:
带屏眼镜的系统界面与应用界面、硬件共同构成用户体验。设计时，需要了解以下系统界面元素。

主界面

主界面是用户熟悉的起点，可以包含时钟、天气、通知，以及 Gemini 的视觉反馈。它位于系统的最底层，借鉴手机锁屏，只提供少量与当前情境有关的信息和操作。

  • 唤醒设备或返回时，回到熟悉的界面。
  • 无需操作，就能看到与当前情境有关、一眼可读的信息。
  • 提供用户接下来可能需要的操作入口。
  • 多个活动同时运行时，支持多任务处理。

系统栏

系统栏承载 Gemini 的视觉反馈，以及通知、提醒、胶囊提示、时钟等次要但一眼可读的信息。除通知胶囊外，应用不能占用这一区域。不使用时，系统栏不可见，主界面除外。系统栏显示什么内容，取决于用户当前所处的位置：

  • 主界面。
  • 应用界面。

此外，还有一些短暂呈现的内容，可以不受当前位置限制，随时出现，例如悬浮通知（HUN）。

通知

眼镜通知与手机通知类似，内容应简短、及时且与用户相关。通知采用系统模板，并根据是否获得焦点、屏幕是否可用，呈现不同状态。

LED 指示灯

所有带屏眼镜均配有两枚 LED 指示灯，一枚面向佩戴者，一枚面向周围的人。指示灯通过视觉反馈说明功能和设备状态，设计完整体验时也应将它们纳入考虑。这些都是系统界面指示，无法更改。
bodyEn:
The system UI on display glasses weaves together with the app and hardware surfaces. The following are various system UI components to be aware of when designing for display glasses.

Home

Acts as a familiar base for your user. Can contain a clock, weather, notifications, and Gemini visual feedback. Home is the lowest layer of the system. It provides minimal, contextual information and actions, and is inspired by the phone's lock screen.

  • A familiar screen you wake and come back to
  • Contextual, glanceable information without requiring any input
  • Shortcuts to what you likely want to do next
  • Multitasking abilities when multiple activities are running simultaneously

System bar

The system bar houses Gemini visual feedback and secondary, glanceable information like notifications, alerts, chips, and the clock. Apps cannot use this space outside of notifications chips. When not in use, it's invisible (except for home). Content displayed in the system bar depends on its location in the system:

  • Home
  • App view

Additionally, there are ephemeral items that can appear "at any time" across locations. For example: Heads-up Notifications (HUNs), or other locations.

Notifications

Glasses notifications behave like mobile notifications that need to be brief, timely, and relevant. These are templated surfaces that can appear in different states depending on focus and display availability.

LEDs

There are two LEDs on all display glasses, one for the wearer and one for bystanders.   The LED provides visual feedback regarding feature and device states and should be considered when thinking about the holistic user experience. These are system UI indicators and can't be changed.

title: 应用界面
description: 为亮屏、熄屏和无屏状态设计连贯体验，并明确布局、入口与品牌定制的边界。
body:
眼镜上的增强体验是现有手机应用的延伸。你可以设计从手机接续到眼镜的体验。应用可以在无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜上运行。

在带屏眼镜上

带屏眼镜同时提供视觉和声音体验，应用也应同时设计这两类提示。

屏幕亮起时，用户可以通过触控板滚动列表、移动焦点、点击按钮等。此时应提供视觉反馈，避免过多声音反馈造成感官负担。

屏幕熄灭时，应用可以感知屏幕的亮灭状态，让用户在有屏和纯声音体验之间自然切换。

自动熄屏

用户可以按显示键关闭屏幕，也可以等待屏幕超时后自动熄灭。自动熄屏时间可由用户设置，也可由应用定制。只有在这对应用体验至关重要时才应定制，因为它可能影响性能。

在无屏眼镜上

没有显示屏时，应用需要适配纯声音体验。

  • 将输入直接映射到关键操作，例如轻点播放或暂停，向后滑动结束体验。由于没有屏幕上的独立界面元素可供逐个操作，用户无法像在带屏界面上那样浏览选项列表或逐个操作多个按钮，而需要声音提示，并可配合相应的输入方式。详见输入方式。
  • 将视觉提示转换为声音提示。
  • 用户可能使用带屏眼镜，也可能使用仅支持声音的眼镜，因此应用需要同时设计视觉流程和声音流程。

例如，带屏眼镜启动应用后会加载可视界面；无屏眼镜则通过声音提示，引导用户进行作用于整个应用的操作。

在这个例子中，带屏眼镜通过可视界面暂停播报；纯声音模式则通过轻点硬件控件暂停。

了解如何为眼镜开发声音交互。

应用界面的结构

眼镜界面从下向上布局，为用户视野补充信息，并尽量避免遮挡。

  • 设计应用时，将元素锚定在画布底部，再向上排列。
  • 内容应避免上下居中。呈现的内容要精简，呈现方式也要经过仔细考虑，以减少对用户视野的干扰。
  • 通过纵深表达视觉层级。
  • 除通知外，应用不能使用系统栏空间。系统栏不用时不可见。
  • 应用可以滚动，但应尽量减少条目数量，降低认知负担和在镜框上操作的次数。
  • 平衡语音交互与实体手势的使用量；有些时候，实体手势更合适。

进入应用的方式

眼镜应用是主应用体验的延伸，因此目前应将手机接续作为主要入口。随着眼镜形态逐步成熟，可以预期未来会出现来自系统界面或 AI 能力的入口。

从手机接续到眼镜

通过手机启动眼镜上的应用，可以由用户明确触发，也可以在任务流程中自然接续。

自然接续是用户流程中的自然一步，可自动启动部分眼镜体验。例如，开始导航后，在眼镜上显示逐向指引；开始播放媒体后，在眼镜上显示播放状态。

明确触发需要用户在手机应用中操作，才启动眼镜体验，例如从应用中打开摄像头，或点击启动眼镜应用的按钮。入口应使用眼镜图标清楚标识，也可搭配“在眼镜上打开”的文字。

定制应用外观

眼镜应用在用户体验和界面设计上保留了灵活性。

框架提供经过充分优化的基础组件，例如列表和卡片，以及基础样式、色彩和文字排版。任何定制都应经过审慎考虑，服务于信息表达或品牌识别。

进一步了解 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 视觉样式。
bodyEn:
Augmented experiences on glasses are an extension of your existing mobile app, you can create handoff experiences from your mobile app to Glasses. Your app can run on both audio glasses and display glasses.

On display glasses

Display glasses provide a visual and audio experience, your app experience should include both visual and audio cues.

When the display is on, the user can interact with the touchpad to scroll lists, move focus, click buttons, etc. Show visual feedback to not overwhelm the user's senses with over providing audio feedback.

When the display is off, your app can keep track of whether the display is on or off, so your user can go from a display to audio experience and back.

Display timeout

Users can turn the display off by pressing the display button, or wait for the display to timeout. Timeout can be configured by users or customized for your app. Only customize if crucial to your app's experience as this can have performance impacts.

On audio glasses

Displayless adapts to an audio-only experience.

  • Input is mapped to key actions, like playing or pausing with a tap and ending experiences by swiping back. Since there is no UI elements to individually interact with on a display. For example, on displayless the user can't scroll through a list of options and multiple buttons, instead they will need an audio cue with a possible corresponding input. Read more on input.
  • Translate visual cues to audio cues.
  • Your users may have display or audio-only glasses, this is why it's important to consider audio and visual flows for your app.

For example, on display glasses, a visual UI would load after the app is launched, while on audio glasses, an audio cue prompts the user on an app-wide interaction.

Here the audio readout is paused by visual UI on display glasses, while a hardware input tap pauses for audio-only.

How to build audio interactions for glasses.

App anatomy

The Glasses interface builds from the bottom up to augment rather than block a user's line of sight.

  • When designing your app, anchor elements to the bottom of the canvas, to build upwards.
  • Content should avoid being centered vertically and remain minimal and thoughtful as to be less distracting in the user's vision.
  • Depth is used for visual hierarchy.
  • Outside of notifications, apps cannot use the system bar space. When not in use, it's invisible.
  • Apps can scroll, but try to keep the number of items minimal to reduce cognitive load and minimize on-frame interactions.
  • Balance the amount of voice interaction needed versus physical gestures, sometimes a physical gesture is preferred.

Entry points

Since your glasses app is an extension to your core app experience, consider handoff from the phone as the current primary entry point. You should expect future entry points from the system UI or AI capabilities as the glasses form factor matures.

Handoff from phone

Start an app on your glasses from your phone with an explicit action or implicit handoff.

Implicit handoff can occur automatically as a natural part of a user flow to launch part of the glasses experience. For example, starting navigation displays turn-by-turn on glasses or media playback has a visual indication on glasses.

Explicit handoff requires a user interaction within the mobile app to launch the glasses experience. For example, toggling the camera on from the app or a button that launches the glasses app. Clearly indicate with an eyeglasses icon and optional "Launch on glasses" label.

Customization

Apps on glasses provide flexibility over the user experience and UI design. 

The UI framework provides a highly-optimized base set of components, like lists and cards, and base styles, color and typography. Any customization should be thoughtfully done to help communicate to your users or reflect your brand.

text: 眼镜上的增强体验是现有手机应用的延伸。你可以设计从手机接续到眼镜的体验。应用可以在无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜上运行。 在带屏眼镜上 带屏眼镜同时提供视觉和声音体验，应用也应同时设计这两类提示。 屏幕亮起时 ，用户可以通过触控板滚动列表、移动焦点、点击按钮等。此时应提供视觉反馈，避免过多声音反馈造成感官负担。 屏幕熄灭时 ，应用可以感知屏幕的亮灭状态，让用户在有屏和纯声音体验之间自然切换。 自动熄屏 用户可以按显示键关闭屏幕，也可以等待屏幕超时后自动熄灭。自动熄屏时间可由用户设置，也可由应用定制。只有在这对应用体验至关重要时才应定制，因为它可能影响性能。 在无屏眼镜上 没有显示屏时，应用需要适配纯声音体验。 将输入直接映射到关键操作，例如轻点播放或暂停，向后滑动结束体验。由于没有屏幕上的独立界面元素可供逐个操作，用户无法像在带屏界面上那样浏览选项列表或逐个操作多个按钮，而需要声音提示，并可配合相应的输入方式。详见 输入方式 。 将视觉提示转换为声音提示。 用户可能使用带屏眼镜，也可能使用仅支持声音的眼镜，因此应用需要同时设计视觉流程和声音流程。 例如，带屏眼镜启动应用后会加载可视界面；无屏眼镜则通过声音提示，引导用户进行作用于整个应用的操作。 在这个例子中，带屏眼镜通过可视界面暂停播报；纯声音模式则通过轻点硬件控件暂停。 了解如何 为眼镜开发声音交互 。 应用界面的结构 眼镜界面从下向上布局，为用户视野补充信息，并尽量避免遮挡。 设计应用时，将元素锚定在画布底部，再向上排列。 内容应避免上下居中。呈现的内容要精简，呈现方式也要经过仔细考虑，以减少对用户视野的干扰。 通过 纵深 表达视觉层级。 除通知外，应用不能使用系统栏空间。系统栏不用时不可见。 应用可以滚动，但应尽量减少条目数量，降低认知负担和在镜框上操作的次数。 平衡语音交互与实体手势的使用量；有些时候，实体手势更合适。 进入应用的方式 眼镜应用是主应用体验的延伸，因此目前应将手机接续作为主要入口。随着眼镜形态逐步成熟，可以预期未来会出现来自系统界面或 AI 能力的入口。 从手机接续到眼镜 通过手机启动眼镜上的应用，可以由用户明确触发，也可以在任务流程中自然接续。 自然接续 是用户流程中的自然一步，可自动启动部分眼镜体验。例如，开始导航后，在眼镜上显示逐向指引；开始播放媒体后，在眼镜上显示播放状态。 明确触发 需要用户在手机应用中操作，才启动眼镜体验，例如从应用中打开摄像头，或点击启动眼镜应用的按钮。入口应使用眼镜图标清楚标识，也可搭配“在眼镜上打开”的文字。 定制应用外观 眼镜应用在用户体验和界面设计上保留了灵活性。 框架提供经过充分优化的基础组件，例如 列表 和 卡片 ，以及基础样式、 色彩 和 文字排版 。任何定制都应经过审慎考虑，服务于信息表达或品牌识别。 进一步了解 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 视觉样式 。

title: 在应用中使用 AI
description: 在充分尊重用户意愿的前提下，让多模态情境信息帮助 AI 更自然地完成任务。
body:
无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜能以第一人称视角、多模态信息呈现用户与环境的互动。结合语音输入和硬件传感器，这有望为应用提供前所未有的丰富情境信息。要利用这些信息，可以在应用中集成智能体，把多模态输入交给大语言模型。你可以使用 Gemini Live API，也可以集成自定义 AI 智能体。

负责任地使用 AI

设计应照顾用户各方面的舒适感，包括感官、认知、社交，以及与 AI 相处时的自在程度。

应用应遵循“先征得同意，再采取行动”的原则：

  • 不要因为应用已经打开，就默认可以开始录制。
  • 启用传感器前，应有明确触发，例如用户做出实体手势。
  • 如果智能体认为当前任务需要摄像头，应先询问用户是否开启。
  • 只收集提供价值所必需的最少数据，完成处理后及时丢弃。

智能体的设计考量

在无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜上，AI 可以高效完成文字转语音、图像识别等任务，并让用户通过自然语言交流，无需沿固定的对话分支逐步操作。

自然的声音提示和轻量的视觉信息，可以帮助用户更顺畅地在手机与眼镜之间完成任务。

在应用中集成智能体时，应考虑：

  • 表达方式与语气。
  • 用户日常生活中的具体情境。
  • 用户安全。
  • 避免信息或交互过多，给用户造成负担。
  • 让用户在社交场合也能自在地使用。

AI 智能体应简洁、少打扰，遵循对话体验的最佳实践和AI 交互模式。
bodyEn:
Audio and display glasses provide a first-person and muli-modal view of the user interacting with their environment. Combined with voice input and hardware sensors, this has the potential to provide an unprecedented level of contextual information to your app. To utilize this context in your app, you can use an in-app agent and route these multi-modal inputs to your LLM. Your app can take advantage of the Gemini Live API or integrate a custom AI agent.

Use AI Responsibly

Design for all aspects of user comfort, including Sensory, Cognitive, Social, and Comfort with AI.

Design your apps for 'Consent First':

  • Don't assume you can record because an app is open.
  • Use explicit triggers like a physical gesture before activating sensors.
  • Have your agent ask to turn on the camera if it deems it necessary for the activity.
  • Collect the minimum amount of data necessary to deliver value, process it, and then discard it.

Design considerations for your agent

For audio and display glasses, AI features provide an efficient manner to accomplish tasks like text to speech and image recognition. AI allows for interaction through natural language, instead of static trees.

AI can help make completing tasks between phone and glasses more natural with natural audio cues and subtle visuals.

When integrating an agent within your app, consider:

  • Voice and tone
  • Contexts of the user in everyday life
  • User safety
  • Don't overwhelm the user
  • Design for social comfort

The AI agent should be concise and unobtrusive, following conversational UX best practices and AI patterns

title: 输入方式
description: 明确系统与应用各自处理的输入，让手势简单、反馈及时、退出始终可达。
body:
眼镜支持多种交互输入，包括硬件控件与触控、身体手势，以及语音。

硬件控件

不同型号的眼镜可能采用不同控件，但多数会包括相机键、触控板、显示键，以及电源开关或电源键。硬件控件有默认的操作含义，其中部分可以重新映射到应用操作。与触摸屏相比，眼镜输入更偏向一维操作：用户一次通常只进行一种控制输入。默认输入映射中，有些由应用处理，有些由系统处理。

以下输入由系统处理：

  • 相机键单按拍照，长按录像。
  • 在触控板上双指滑动，调节音量。
  • 长按触控板，或通过麦克风说出唤醒词，启动 Gemini。
  • 在带屏眼镜上，向下滑动被系统解释为“返回”。

应用可以使用的输入与硬件能力包括：

  • 触控板单指滑动。
  • 麦克风。
  • 第一视角（POV）摄像头。
  • 惯性测量单元（IMU）。
  • 相机键双按。

无屏眼镜

输入控件手势对应操作
触控板（1）轻点播放／暂停／确认
触控板（1）滑动下一项／上一项／关闭
触控板（1）向下滑动不适用
触控板（1）长按唤起 AI
触控板（1）双指滑动调节音量
显示键（2）按下不适用
相机键（3）按下拍照／结束录像
相机键（3）长按开始录像
相机键（3）双按相机操作

带屏眼镜

输入控件手势对应操作
触控板（1）轻点播放／暂停／确认
触控板（1）滑动界面导航
触控板（1）向下滑动返回
触控板（1）长按唤起 AI
触控板（1）双指滑动调节音量
显示键（2）按下唤醒／休眠
相机键（3）按下拍照／结束录像
相机键（3）长按开始录像
相机键（3）双按相机操作

易用性原则

设计眼镜输入时，应遵循以下原则。

操作短促、迅速，不显突兀

无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜都适合简短、快速的手势，而非复杂、精细的控制。

推荐

采用快速手势，让用户在外出活动时也能自然地操作。

避免

要求用户完成手机或电脑上那样复杂、精确的手势。

让用户看得懂，减少记忆负担

对于带屏眼镜，应限制需要记忆的手势数量，并利用用户已有的操作习惯和理解。

推荐

显示屏可用时，提供可见的界面元素，帮助用户完成操作。

避免

明明有显示屏，仍过度依赖用户记住手势。

随时提供立即退出的方式

用户应能在任何时候退出眼镜上的当前体验。

立即、清楚地反馈识别到的手势与执行的操作

对无屏眼镜而言，声音输出和提示音都是重要的手势反馈。提示音应在手势后立即响起，并在不同环境下都能听见、辨认。

带屏眼镜采用间接交互方式，即时的视觉反馈能显著提升易用性。

帮助用户少出错，操作更顺畅

通过以下方式预防误操作：

  • 免去记忆负担。
  • 考虑可能发生的无意误操作。
  • 支持撤销操作。
  • 重要操作前给予提醒。

推荐

将初始焦点放在误操作代价较低的选项上，例如接听来电。

避免

将初始焦点放在误操作代价较高的选项上，例如拒接来电。
bodyEn:
Glasses have multiple sources and types of interaction inputs, including hardware and touch, physical gesture, and voice.

Hardware controls

Glasses controls can vary depending on device model, but most will include a camera button, touchpad, display button, and power switch or button. Hardware controls have default interactions, and some can be remapped for your app. Consider that inputs for glasses are more 1-dimensional, where users can make one control input at a time, compared to touchscreen inputs. The glasses hardware controls have default interaction mapping, some of which are handled by the app, and others that are handled by the system.

The system will handle the following inputs:

  • Camera button single press to take photos and camera button hold to take videos
  • Swiping with two fingers on the touchpad for volume
  • Touch & hold on the touchpad and the wake word on the microphone will launch Gemini
  • System interprets swipe down on display glasses as system back.

Your app has access to the glasses:

  • Single-finger swipe on touchpad
  • Microphone
  • Point-of-View (POV) camera
  • Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)
  • Camera button double-press

Audio glasses

Input Gesture Interaction affect
Touchpad (1) Tap Play / Pause / Confirm
Swipe Next/Previous/Dismiss
Swipe down N/A
Touch & hold Invoke AI
2-finger swipe Volume
Display button (2) Press N/A
Camera button (3) Press Photo / Video end
Touch & hold Video start
Double press Camera

Display glasses

Input Gesture Interaction affect
Touchpad (1) Tap Play / Pause / Confirm
Swipe UI Navigation
Swipe down Back
Touch & hold Invoke AI
2-finger swipe Volume
Display button (2) Press Wake/Sleep
Camera button (3) Press Photo / Video end
Touch & hold Video start
Double press Camera

On display focus states have a visual affordances.

Usability principles

Use the following principles when designing for glasses inputs:

Input interaction is quick & discreet

Audio and display glasses are designed around short and quick gestures rather than complex and precise controls.

Do

Design around fast gestures that don't feel out of place while a user is out and about.

Don't

Expect complex and precise gestures like those on mobile and desktop.

Recognition rather than recall for display glasses

Limit the number of gestures that the user needs to remember, and take advantage of existing user mental models.

Do

Provide UI elements for users to complete actions when the display is available.

Don't

Overly rely on users remembering gestures if the display is available.

Always provide an immediate exit for users

A user should be able to exit an experience on their glasses at any point.

Provide immediate, clear feedback about detected gesture and action taken

For audio glasses, both audio output and earcons are crucial for gesture feedback. Earcons should be played immediately after a gesture, be audible, and be distinct in various environments.

For display glasses, immediate visual feedback significantly enhances usability due to the indirect interaction paradigm.

Promote a smooth experience

Help users avoid mistakes by:

  • Removing memory burdens
  • Accounting for possible accidental slips
  • Supporting undo actions
  • Warning users before important actions

Do

Put initial focus on a lower-cost action, like accepting a call.

Don't

Put initial focus on high-cost actions, like declining a call.

title: 权限申请
description: 将授权交给手机完成，并清楚解释用途、影响与后续修改方式。
body:
当应用需要获得眼镜相关权限时，应引导用户前往手机，在手机上的权限对话框中完成授权。

后续遵循手机应用的权限最佳实践：

  • 先向用户说明为什么需要这些权限，以及授权情况可能如何影响功能。
  • 提供之后修改权限偏好的入口。

进一步了解如何申请硬件权限。
bodyEn:
When an app needs permissions to be granted the glasses, it should direct the user to the phone where a permissions dialog will display.

From there, follow permissions best practices for mobile:

  • Prime the user, so they know why the permissions are asked and possible implications to features.
  • Provide a way to update permissions preferences later.

Read more on how to request hardware permissions.

title: 导航与退出
description: 保持浅层导航，提供清楚的返回与退出方式，并考虑误退出造成的进度损失。
body:
眼镜上的导航应与其他 Android 设备一样熟悉。应用可以沿用许多常见模式，例如滑动浏览媒体内容，以及通过返回栈逐级返回。

眼镜应用较为简单，导航层级也应尽量少。

用滑动切换内容

让滑动在各类内容中保持一致的含义：横向切换。对无屏眼镜而言，这里的内容是媒体；对带屏眼镜而言，则是可视界面。

在应用内返回

系统返回手势让用户在应用的界面层级中退回一步。到达应用最外层后，再返回就进入主界面。尽量减少层级，以降低认知负担，让用户快速回到主界面。

无屏眼镜的返回由系统处理；带屏眼镜可定制返回行为。在带屏眼镜的触控板上向下滑动，会触发系统返回。

结束眼镜上的当前活动

让用户能够结束当前活动并退出应用。对于通话、翻译和 Gemini 等连续音频体验，向后滑动后立即结束通常最合适。对于持续时间较长、误退出会丢失进度的活动，应考虑增加一步确认。

无屏眼镜使用向后滑动退出。应用不播放通用的退出提示音；如需退出反馈，仅使用可选的语音结束小结。

对于结束通话、停止锻炼等破坏性操作，应考虑二次确认。例如：

  1. 用户向后滑动，应用播报：“结束徒步吗？再返回一次以确认。”
  2. 用户再次向后滑动，应用播报：“徒步已结束。你共走了 2.8 英里。”
  3. 播报结束后，再调用退出活动的操作。

带屏眼镜在结束活动的方式上有更大灵活性。在界面中放置按钮，清楚地提供退出入口。
bodyEn:
Navigating on glasses should feel just as familiar as with other Android form factors. Your app can use many of the same navigation patterns, like swipe to navigate media content and back stack. 

Due to the simplicity of Glasses apps, navigation should remain shallow.

Swipes to navigate content

This model aligns swipe as a way for the user to navigate lateral through all types of content. On Audio glasses, media is content. On Display glasses, visual UI is content.

In-App Back

The system back gesture lets users move back a step in the app layer stack. Once on the top-most app surface, the system back will navigate to Home. Keep the levels minimal to reduce cognitive load and allow the user to navigate home quickly.

Back is handled by the system on displayless glasses, but can be customized for display. On display glasses, swiping down on the touchpad will perform a system back.

Ending your glasses activity

Let the user end the current activity and exit your app. Ending on swipe-back immediately is best for continuous audio streams like calls, translation, and Gemini. Consider introducing a second confirmation step for longer activities where accidentally ending the session would lose progress.

On audio glasses, use swipe-back as the method for exiting. Apps don't play a generic exit earcon; keep exit signals limited to optional, spoken activity wrap-ups.

For destructive actions like ending a call or stopping a workout, consider a secondary confirmation. For example:

  1. The user swipes back and the app reads out, "End hike? Go back again to confirm."
  2. The user swipes back again: "Hike ended. You walked 2.8 miles."
  3. Call exit activity when finished reading out.

On display glasses, you have much more flexibility for how to end your activity. Place a button in your interface to make a clear exit affordance.

title: AI 交互模式
description: 让对话、暂停、多模态输入和环境感知共同服务于自然、可控的 AI 体验。
body:
无屏眼镜与带屏眼镜高度贴近个人和具体情境，与不断发展的 AI 交互方式结合，为新的交互设计带来独特机会。你可以使用摄像头、麦克风、触控板等设备能力，在舒适与用户安全的原则下，探索 AI、应用和眼镜之间的新交互。

眼镜把 AI 带到用户的眼前和耳边。设计这类体验时，应考虑这样的交互模式：让 AI 作为助手，配合一眼可读的视觉信息提供帮助。

自然对话

AI 模型支持持续的自然语言交流，不必局限于短暂交接或固定的对话树。应优先设计实时、连续且有帮助的对话，而不是一段段短会话。

暂停与停止

允许用户休息，随时打断对话或任务。用户可以通过触碰、手势或语音实现。智能体可以继续监听后续交互信号，并通过向用户学习，形成适合用户的续接方式。用户应能在无屏眼镜上向后滑动退出会话，在带屏眼镜上向下滑动退出。

多模态协同

眼镜可以将多种硬件能力与 AI 配合使用，提供更丰富的体验。例如，在对话中允许用户启用摄像头，让 AI 了解周围环境并提供情境帮助。

不要让摄像头持续运行，这会影响续航；应由用户在需要额外输入时启用。

关注用户所处的环境

AI 声音交互可以按需补充信息或重复回答。有显示屏时，可提供与当前情境相关的视觉界面，并与声音输出配合。信息应清晰、一眼可读，让用户继续专注于真实世界。
bodyEn:
Audio and display glasses provide a unique opportunity for new interaction design with the overlap of a new, highly-contextual and personal form factor with evolving AI patterns. You have access to the device's hardware and features, including camera, microphone, and touchpad, to fully explore new interaction patterns between AI, your app, and glasses with comfort and user safety principles in mind.

Audio and display glasses bring AI capabilities to the user's eyes and ears. When designing these experiences, consider patterns that recognize AI as an assistant with glanceable visuals.

Natural conversation

AI models allow for ongoing natural language interaction instead of short handoffs or static conversation trees. Prioritize live ongoing helpful conversations with agents rather than short sessions.

Pause and stop

Allow the user to take a break and interrupt the conversation or task. This may be a physical touch, gesture, or spoken interaction. Your agent could continue to listen for additional interaction cues and establish a custom pattern to continue by learning from the user.  Allow users to exit the session by swiping back on audio glasses, or swiping down on display glasses.

Multi-modal

Glasses can use multiple hardware features together with AI to bring richer experiences. For example, you can use the camera for contextual assistance by allowing the user to activate the camera during your conversation to understand the world around them.

Don't keep the camera running as it impacts battery performance, instead allow the user to activate the camera for additional input.

Environmental awareness

AI audio interactions can provide additional information or repeat responses as needed. Consider providing visuals when a display is available as contextual UI that harmonizes with audio output. Allow the user to remain focused in the real world, providing glanceable legible information.

title: 使用引导
description: 在恰当时机介绍眼镜功能，覆盖多种入口、必要授权、使用教学与异常恢复。
body:
智能眼镜可以用新的方式延伸手机应用体验。在合适的时机介绍功能、教会用户使用，让眼镜自然地成为手机应用的一部分。使用引导应帮助用户完成必要授权，知道如何在眼镜上启动体验，并掌握应用相关功能。通用的应用引导与身份验证设计，请参阅手机应用使用引导。

何时引导，在哪里引导

眼镜的使用引导可以包括：

  • 检测眼镜。
  • 在眼镜和手机上发现可用功能。
  • 设置权限。
  • 学习使用方法。

这些流程可以在用到功能时出现，也可以预先集中进行；可以在眼镜中进行，也可以在配套应用中进行。

用到时再引导

介绍眼镜相关功能时，应优先采用适时引导：当用户在应用中遇到该功能时，再说明用法并申请权限。

这样，用户可以在功能与自己更相关、也更适合使用时了解它，不容易忘记。这也是更适合回访用户的方式：用户首次配对眼镜后重新进入应用时，就可以触发功能介绍。

预先集中引导

功能教学和权限申请也可以在应用的使用引导或欢迎流程中预先集中进行。以下情况可能适合这种方式：

  • 眼镜能力是应用核心体验不可或缺的一部分。
  • 用户马上就会使用相关功能。
  • 计划安排较长的使用教学流程。

用户在完成引导后可能会忘记这些内容，因此可以从说明功能价值或提供信息的角度来设计这个阶段。

如果眼镜引导只是整个使用引导流程的一部分，可以根据情况决定：检测到眼镜后，是否告诉用户眼镜已可用。

注意：引导步骤过多，可能使用户放弃完成流程。

在眼镜上进行引导

用户可以从眼镜启动应用。首次使用时，应给予欢迎提示、引导完成必要授权，并说明如何使用眼镜相关功能。

推荐

用简洁的声音和视觉反馈，说明特色功能的使用方法。

避免

在眼镜上安排注册等复杂流程。应将用户引导到手机完成。

通过配套应用进行引导

配套应用是眼镜的设置、支持与偏好管理中心。用户在这里配对眼镜，学习基本操作。既然配套应用已经介绍如何配对、使用眼镜和 Gemini，你的应用就不应重复这些基础知识，而应聚焦自身功能。配套应用还通过 Google Play 商店提供发现应用的入口。

首次设置

用户可能从多个入口发现并开始使用眼镜功能，设计时应覆盖这些路径。只要满足相应条件，就应提供首次使用体验。例如，用户此前已经完成手机应用的使用引导，但当时尚未配对眼镜；之后配对成功，再次进入应用，这正是介绍眼镜功能的合适时机。

从手机应用开始

在手机应用中检测到已配对的眼镜后，先介绍可用功能，再说明使用方法与权限用途。用户完成授权后，将体验接续到眼镜。

进一步了解权限申请。

提示：如果用户通过眼镜相关请求、分享链接或 Google Play 商店安装应用，应通过深层链接直接进入眼镜功能流程。例如，下载完成且用户授予权限后，介绍眼镜功能并开展使用教学。

可在 Android Onboarding Figma Kit 中查看引导示例。

从眼镜开始

如果用户首次从眼镜启动应用的眼镜端活动，应先说明所需权限及用途，再引导用户到手机授权。完成后，可在手机应用内提供更直观的使用演示，也可以在眼镜端活动中继续引导。

如果应用接入了 Gemini，但用户尚未下载 Gemini 应用，应先提示用户在手机上下载。

可以通过声音提示、提示音和手势提示，在眼镜端活动中进行教学；也应考虑，是否用一次集中的用法说明就能讲得更清楚。

无论采用哪种教学方式，用户首次进入眼镜端活动时，都应有声音欢迎提示。

使用教学

清楚说明如何使用眼镜端活动，不要让用户猜测功能在哪里、该如何操作。

结合当前情境、在需要时出现的教学，可以告诉用户眼镜功能的入口及用途。

教学流程应突出：

  • 值得尝试的特色唤起方式或操作。
  • 特有的输入映射或手势。
  • 如需使用摄像头或麦克风，应提醒用户会用到这些功能，并解释应用为什么需要它们。

避免

让用户猜测有哪些功能。应主动提供可以尝试的操作建议或指引。

功能介绍不必集中在某一个时刻。如果用户能在不同时间使用眼镜端活动中的一个或多个功能，应通过引导标记或提示说明指出这些功能。

设计资源

Android Onboarding Figma Kit 提供使用引导模板、用户流程和教学素材。也可以下载眼镜使用教学动效的 After Effects 文件，定制并在应用中实现教学动画。

要调整动效素材的颜色，请下载并打开 After Effects 文件：

  1. 打开 Master Color 合成。
  2. 使用颜色区域中的取色点与色彩滑块。
  3. 输入十六进制颜色值。

之后可将动效渲染输出，或导出为 Lottie 格式。

Android Onboarding Figma Kit 包含适用于不同 Android 设备形态的引导示例和静态素材。

复制文件后，前往 Intelligent eyewear Welcome sequence 页面，查看推荐的智能眼镜引导流程。

在 Intelligent eyewear Instructional illustrations 页面，可找到用于手机应用的教学插图素材。

异常与恢复

在使用引导的各个阶段，都应考虑异常处理：

  • 如果眼镜解除配对，提醒用户。
  • 如果用户尚未授予权限，或此前拒绝过权限，应说明情况，并提供直达相应设置的链接，让用户授予权限。
  • 可提供帮助与支持入口，让用户复习或进一步了解眼镜功能。

组件与模式

使用 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 组件、提示音和声音提示，在眼镜端活动中开展使用教学。

  • 眼镜上的使用引导应遵循音频焦点状态。
  • 视觉引导可以使用手势说明、按钮和卡片。
  • 关于手机端的常见布局与组件，请参阅手机应用使用引导。

Intelligent eyewear can extend your app's mobile experience in novel ways. Introduce and educate users on your app's capabilities in the right moment so that their glasses feel like a seamless extension of your mobile app. Follow these best practices while onboarding users, so they have proper permissions, know how to invoke glasses use, and know how to use app-related features. For more on general app onboarding and authentication, refer to mobile user onboarding.

Usage & placement

Glasses onboarding can include:

  • Glasses detection
  • Feature discovery on glasses and on mobile
  • Permissions setup
  • User education

Onboarding related flows can happen contextually, upfront, on glasses, or within the companion app.

Contextual onboarding

When introducing glasses related features, defer to just-in-time, in-app, education and permissions, meaning when a user encounters the feature.

This allows users to learn about features when they are more relevant and usable to them and less likely to forget. This is also preferred for returning users, as the discovery process can trigger when the user returns the first time glasses are paired.

Upfront onboarding

Education and permissions can also be a part of upfront app onboarding (or welcome placement). This approach might make sense if your app's onboarding falls into one of these categories:

  • Glasses integration is essential to your app's core experience
  • Your user will use the feature right away
  • You plan to have a longer user education flow

During upfront onboarding, consider this a value proposition or informative moment, as they may forget after onboarding.

When included as part of a larger onboarding flow, you can decide whether to notify the user that glasses are available if they are detected.

Caution: Adding too many steps to an onboarding process might deter users from completing onboarding.

Onboarding on intelligent eyewear

Users can invoke your app from their glasses. For first-time use, they need to be welcomed, grant appropriate permissions, and be taught how to use the AI glasses features.

Do

Provide succinct audio and visual feedback on how to use unique features.

Don't

Include complex onboarding flows, like registration, on glasses. Instead, hand off to their mobile device.

Onboarding through a companion app

A companion app serves as a setup, support, and preferences hub for a user's AI glasses. This is where they pair their glasses and learn basic usage. Since the companion app teaches users how to pair and use their glasses, along with Gemini, your app shouldn't include such fundamental concepts. Instead, focus on your own app's features. The companion app also provides app discovery with access to the Google Play Store.

First-time setup

Users can find and start using your app's glasses features through several routes, so it's important to account for multiple entry points. These methods should be first-time experiences whenever certain criteria is met. For example, a user might have previously completed onboarding before they paired their glasses and then return to the app with their glasses now paired. This case would be an ideal moment to trigger your glasses feature discovery.

Mobile app

Within the mobile app, if glasses are paired and detected, then prompt feature discovery, followed by education and permission priming. Once the user has granted permissions, hand off to glasses.

For more on permissions.

Note: If a user installs an app from a glasses intent, through sharing or from the Google Play Store, deeplink into a glasses flow. For example, once the app finishes downloading and the user grants permissions, prompt glasses feature discovery and education.

Get an onboarding example with the Android Onboarding Figma Kit.

Intelligent eyewear

If the user starts your app's Glasses activity for the first time from their Glasses, they should be prompted with permissions priming, then hand off to their phone to grant the required permissions. Once complete, you can provide education within your app (for more visual walkthrough), or within the Glasses activity.

If your app is Gemini connected, but the Gemini app isn't downloaded, the user is prompted to download the app on their mobile device first.

You can include user education within the Glasses activity by using audio queues, earcons, and gesture hints, but consider if one modal summary can better convey use.

Regardless of how you handle user education, use an audio queue to welcome your users into the Glasses activity the first time they use it.

Education

Inform users on how to use your Glasses activity, so they don't have to guess on where or how to use it.

Contextual, or just-in-time, education helps inform users where to access and what feature is associated with their glasses.

Within the educational flow, highlight:

  • Specialized invocations or actions to try out.
  • Unique input mappings or gestures.
  • Specialized invocations or actions to try out.
  • Unique input mappings or gestures.

  • If using the camera or microphone, remind users about this use, and explain why your app needs them.

    Don't

    Make users guess on available features. Give users suggestions or directions on what to do.

Feature discovery doesn't have to remain at one point. If they can access one or more features within the glasses activity at different times, point them out with a coachmark or tooltip.

Resources

Discover onboarding templates, user flows, and user education assets in the Android Onboarding Figma Kit or download the glasses user education motion assets After Effects file for customizing and implementing educational motion graphics within your app.

To customize the color tint of the motion assets, download the After Effects file, when open:

  1. Open Master Color composition.

  2. Use the color field reticle and color plane slider.

  3. Enter a hex value.

Motion graphics can then be rendered or exported as lottie format.

The Android Onboarding Figma kit contains onboarding examples and static assets for use across Android form factors.

After duplicating the file, go to the Intelligent eyewear Welcome sequence page for a suggested UX flow on intelligent eyewear.

On the Intelligent eyewear Instructional illustrations page you can find user education assets to use within your mobile app.

Recovery

Account for error handling during the various onboarding phases:

  • If their glasses become unpaired, alert the user.
  • If a user hasn't granted permissions, or they were previously denied, alert the user and deep link to settings where they can request them.
  • Consider including links to help & support to relearn or better understand using their glasses features.

Components & Patterns

Include user education within the Glasses activity using Jetpack Compose Glimmer components, earcons, and audio queues.

  • Onboarding on glasses should follow audio focus states.
  • For visual elements, consider using gesture hints, buttons, and cards.

title: 声音设计
description: 让声音清楚传达信息、确认操作和提醒注意，同时自然融入日常环境。
body:
声音是智能眼镜体验的重要组成部分，对无屏眼镜尤其如此。眼镜本身的视觉或触觉反馈很少，甚至完全没有，因此声音承担了吸引注意、传递信息和回应操作的主要任务。设计的难点在于：既要让声音听起来舒适愉悦，也要让它在开放式聆听环境中清楚可闻。

扬声器就在耳边

手机扬声器通常离用户较远，提示音往往需要让房间另一头的人也能注意到。无屏眼镜的扬声器则紧贴用户耳旁，声音无需传播很远，带来的聆听体验也更贴近个人。用户全天佩戴眼镜，同一种声音每天会听到很多次；反复播放会让刺耳、冗长或过多的声音更加明显。因此，眼镜的声音设计需要更细腻、更克制。

开放式聆听

眼镜不会像耳机那样封住耳道，用户仍能听见交通、交谈等周围声音。眼镜音频必须自然融入环境，不能与现实声音争抢注意，也不能将它们掩盖。

声音设计原则

声音体验应体现以下原则。

每一声都有明确用途

眼镜发出的每个声音，都应至少承担以下三种作用中的一种。如果一个声音没有任何一种用途，就不应该播放。

传达信息：告知用户发生了什么，或某个状态发生了变化，例如电量不足。

确认操作：回应用户的输入，让用户知道操作已经生效，例如确认音量调整。

提醒注意：让用户注意某件事，或采取行动，例如新通知提示。

一个声音可以同时承担多种作用。例如，低电量提示既是在传递信息，也是在提醒用户注意。

眼镜的声音也应与用户其他设备的声音协调配合，有明确用途，而不是重复其他设备已经完成的提示。

让含义符合直觉

声音设计可以利用人对声音的本能反应：让声音的情绪与事件一致，并借助熟悉的现实参照。积极时刻使用轻快的声音，操作失败使用带有负面情绪的声音，让声音与事件的情绪基调一致。相机快门声无需解释，用户一听就知道刚刚拍了照片。

建议：用轻快的声音表达成功

成功或完成操作时，使用积极、轻快的声音。

避免：用欢快的声音表示错误

发生错误时，不要播放欢快的声音。

建议：只为实际问题使用负向声音

只有确实出现问题时，才使用带有负面意味的音调。

避免：用警报式声音报告日常状态

常规状态更新不应使用令人警觉或受惊的声音。

建议：借助熟悉的现实声音

使用用户熟悉的现实参照，例如用快门声表示拍照。

避免：让用户记忆抽象声音

不要设计必须专门学习和记忆含义的抽象声音。

靠声音特征，而非音量

无屏眼镜等贴近耳朵的设备，如果声音过大，可能惊吓用户、造成疲劳，还会让旁人听见。在嘈杂环境中一味提高音量并不有效，而且很快会令人不适。

应通过独特的声音特征建立辨识度，而不是依靠音量。鲜明的音色、能够从环境噪声中凸显的音高范围，以及清晰的包络——干净的起音、短而柔和的尾音——都能让声音在较低音量下依然清楚可辨。这样，提示音在热闹街道上可以被迅速识别，在安静环境里也能保持轻柔、舒适。

尊重用户当下的情境

让声音自然融入日常生活：通知保持简短，其他媒体同时播放时平滑地暂停或让位，醒目的声音信号只留给高优先级警报。相比更新稍有延迟，不合时宜的打断对用户信任的伤害要大得多。

应用与音乐、通话、导航和数字助手共用同一组扬声器，因此声音必须遵循音频焦点规则，与正在播放的其他音频协调共存。

常见使用场景

以下是眼镜声音交互的几个常见例子。

音频焦点变化

应用失去音频焦点后又重新获得焦点时，用语音提示告知用户此前的体验已经恢复，通常会有帮助。

退出应用

关闭应用时，应提供清楚的反馈，让用户确认应用已经关闭。

麦克风静音

用户直接在无屏眼镜上将麦克风静音时，需要即时反馈。提示音标记麦克风开始静音的准确时刻，明确的语音提示则确认当前麦克风状态，帮助建立信任。
bodyEn:
Audio plays a crucial role in the intelligent eyewear experience, especially on audio glasses. With little or no visual or haptic feedback on the glasses themselves, audio is the primary way to get the user's attention, deliver information, and respond to their input. The challenge is designing sounds that feel delightful but are still audible in an open-ear environment.

Close to the ear

Unlike a mobile device, where the speaker sits at a distance and sounds are built to grab attention from across the room, the speakers on audio glasses sit right next to the user's ears. Sound doesn't have to travel far to reach the user, so the experience is far more personal. Users wear glasses all day and hear the same sounds many times a day. Repetition makes anything harsh, long, or overused more noticeable. That calls for subtler, less intrusive design.

Open-ear experience

Unlike headphones, glasses leave the ear unsealed, allowing users to hear surroundings like traffic or conversations. Audio must blend naturally with the environment without competing or masking real-world sounds.

 Sound design principles

The audio experience should embody the following principles.

Every sound has a purpose

Every sound on the glasses should serve at least one of three jobs. If it doesn't do any of them, it shouldn't play.

Communicate information

Tells the user that something has happened or a status has changed, like when the battery is low.

Confirm intent

Acknowledges the user's input so they know it worked. For example, confirming volume adjustment.

Ask for attention

Asks the user to notice something or act on it, like a notification prompt.

Remember that a sound can have multiple purposes, for example : a low battery sound serves as both information and asking for the user's attention.

Glasses audio should also be purposeful and harmonious with the user's other devices, not repeat what they already do.

Straightforward design

Designing for audio can take advantage of people's instinctive responses to sound by matching emotional tone and building on known references. Use uplifting sounds for positive moments and negative sounds for failed interactions to match emotional tone. A camera shutter needs no explanation because everyone knows a photo was just taken.

Do

Use uplifting sounds for success and completion.

Don't

Use a cheerful sound for an error.

Do

Use negative-sounding tones only for real problems.

Don't

Use alarming or startling tones for routine status.

Do

Build on familiar real-world references, like a shutter for a photo.

Don't

Make abstract sounds the user has to memorize and learn their meaning.

Character over loudness

Close-range sounds can startle users, like on audio glasses, can cause fatigue, and leak audio to others if too loud. Increasing volume is ineffective in loud environments and quickly becomes uncomfortable.

Rather than relying on volume, differentiate sounds through their unique character. Key qualities like a distinct timbre, a pitch range that stands over environmental noise, and a well-defined envelope—featuring a clean attack and a brief, gentle tail—allow sounds to remain clear and noticeable at lower levels. This ensures audio is instantly recognizable on a bustling street while remaining subtle and comfortable in quiet surroundings.

Respect the moment

Integrate audio seamlessly into everyday context: keep notifications succinct, pause or yield gracefully when concurrent media plays, and reserve prominent signals strictly for high-priority alerts. Interrupting at an inappropriate moment undermines user trust far more than a delayed update.

Because apps share a unified speaker output alongside music, phone calls, navigation, and digital assistants, sounds must actively adhere to audio focus rules and coexist harmoniously with active streams.

Common use cases

Here are a few examples of audio patterns for glasses.

Focus change

If an app loses audio focus and regains it, it's often useful to trigger a voice alert to inform users that their experience has resumed.

Exiting an app

When closing an app, it's important to give the user clear feedback to ensure they know the app has closed.

Mute

Muting directly from audio glasses requires immediate feedback. Earcons reinforce the exact moment the mic becomes muted, while explicit voice alerts confirm microphone status and build user trust.

避免：让用户记忆抽象声音

text: 声音是智能眼镜体验的重要组成部分，对无屏眼镜尤其如此。眼镜本身的视觉或触觉反馈很少，甚至完全没有，因此声音承担了吸引注意、传递信息和回应操作的主要任务。设计的难点在于：既要让声音听起来舒适愉悦，也要让它在开放式聆听环境中清楚可闻。 扬声器就在耳边 手机扬声器通常离用户较远，提示音往往需要让房间另一头的人也能注意到。无屏眼镜的扬声器则紧贴用户耳旁，声音无需传播很远，带来的聆听体验也更贴近个人。用户全天佩戴眼镜，同一种声音每天会听到很多次；反复播放会让刺耳、冗长或过多的声音更加明显。因此，眼镜的声音设计需要更细腻、更克制。 开放式聆听 眼镜不会像耳机那样封住耳道，用户仍能听见交通、交谈等周围声音。眼镜音频必须自然融入环境，不能与现实声音争抢注意，也不能将它们掩盖。 声音设计原则 声音体验应体现以下原则。 每一声都有明确用途 眼镜发出的每个声音，都应至少承担以下三种作用中的一种。如果一个声音没有任何一种用途，就不应该播放。 传达信息： 告知用户发生了什么，或某个状态发生了变化，例如电量不足。 确认操作： 回应用户的输入，让用户知道操作已经生效，例如确认音量调整。 提醒注意： 让用户注意某件事，或采取行动，例如新通知提示。 一个声音可以同时承担多种作用。例如，低电量提示既是在传递信息，也是在提醒用户注意。 眼镜的声音也应与用户其他设备的声音协调配合，有明确用途，而不是重复其他设备已经完成的提示。 让含义符合直觉 声音设计可以利用人对声音的本能反应：让声音的情绪与事件一致，并借助熟悉的现实参照。积极时刻使用轻快的声音，操作失败使用带有负面情绪的声音，让声音与事件的情绪基调一致。相机快门声无需解释，用户一听就知道刚刚拍了照片。 建议：用轻快的声音表达成功 成功或完成操作时，使用积极、轻快的声音。 避免：用欢快的声音表示错误 发生错误时，不要播放欢快的声音。 建议：只为实际问题使用负向声音 只有确实出现问题时，才使用带有负面意味的音调。 避免：用警报式声音报告日常状态 常规状态更新不应使用令人警觉或受惊的声音。 建议：借助熟悉的现实声音 使用用户熟悉的现实参照，例如用快门声表示拍照。 避免：让用户记忆抽象声音 不要设计必须专门学习和记忆含义的抽象声音。 靠声音特征，而非音量 无屏眼镜等贴近耳朵的设备，如果声音过大，可能惊吓用户、造成疲劳，还会让旁人听见。在嘈杂环境中一味提高音量并不有效，而且很快会令人不适。 应通过独特的声音特征建立辨识度，而不是依靠音量。鲜明的音色、能够从环境噪声中凸显的音高范围，以及清晰的包络——干净的起音、短而柔和的尾音——都能让声音在较低音量下依然清楚可辨。这样，提示音在热闹街道上可以被迅速识别，在安静环境里也能保持轻柔、舒适。 尊重用户当下的情境 让声音自然融入日常生活：通知保持简短，其他媒体同时播放时平滑地暂停或让位，醒目的声音信号只留给高优先级警报。相比更新稍有延迟，不合时宜的打断对用户信任的伤害要大得多。 应用与音乐、通话、导航和数字助手共用同一组扬声器，因此声音必须遵循音频焦点规则，与正在播放的其他音频协调共存。 常见使用场景 以下是眼镜声音交互的几个常见例子。 音频焦点变化 应用失去音频焦点后又重新获得焦点时，用语音提示告知用户此前的体验已经恢复，通常会有帮助。 退出应用 关闭应用时，应提供清楚的反馈，让用户确认应用已经关闭。 麦克风静音 用户直接在无屏眼镜上将麦克风静音时，需要即时反馈。提示音标记麦克风开始静音的准确时刻，明确的语音提示则确认当前麦克风状态，帮助建立信任。

title: 提示音
description: 用简短声音反馈操作与状态，并遵循系统在隐私、相机和关键警报上的优先级。
body:
提示音（Earcon，audio icon“声音图标”的简称）用简短的声音向用户传递提示或反馈。眼镜为常见交互提供了提示音。

提示音与视觉图标一样，需要用户学习和记忆，因此应谨慎使用。不要让应用的声音含义与已有的系统提示音发生冲突。

  • 如果一句自然语言就能说清，不要换成还需要额外解释的提示音。
  • 不要制作模仿系统声音的自定义提示音，以免用户混淆。
  • 用户通常在执行具体操作时，逐渐学会提示音的含义。
  • 提示音应简单、直观。
  • 与音频提示（audio alerts）相比，提示音能描述的信息更少。

应用也会沿用手机端的提示音，因此眼镜端与手机端的声音应保持一致，让整体声音体验简洁统一。例如，同一应用在手机和眼镜上可以共用静音提示音。

系统提示音

系统默认提供一些通用声音，设计应用时应将它们纳入考虑，例如：

隐私与关键警报提示音

关键硬件警报和隐私提示音的优先级高于所有其他音频。麦克风静音提示属于由系统控制的隐私提示音。

系统声音行为
麦克风静音 / 取消静音由系统控制的隐私提示音。
电量严重不足
  • 播放音量不低于硬件音量的 20%。
  • 不受“勿扰模式”限制。
  • 与手机断开连接时仍会播放。
  • 完全压制其他所有音频流，包括正在进行的电话通话。
触发过热保护
设备断开连接 / 链路丢失

相机提示音

所有相机和快门提示音都是不可静音的系统声音。播放音量不低于硬件音量的 60%，并且不受“勿扰模式”限制，以保护佩戴者和周围人的隐私。

当视频通话、视觉辅助等应用请求开启眼镜朝前的相机视频流时，系统会播放一组不可静音的提示。在视频流开启前告知用户，并留出取消操作的机会：

  1. 启动提示：播放不可静音的提示音，告知用户有应用正在请求开启朝前相机的视频流。
  2. 3 秒倒计时：在视频流开启前，播放可听见的 3 秒倒计时，让用户有时间在需要时取消倒计时或取消相机访问。
  3. 视频流开启：视频流正式开启时，播放不可静音的相机开启提示音。
  4. 视频流关闭 / 用户取消：视频流关闭或用户取消倒计时时，播放统一的不可静音提示音。

应用提示音

提示音可以用于应用中的多种场景。以下功能的提示音不会默认提供，设计时可以考虑为它们加入声音反馈：

通用提示音

通用提示音是在不同应用间共用的标准声音，帮助用户形成统一的声音语义。应用应使用这里提供的声音资源。

操作用途音频
打开应用应用打开时，用提示音迎接用户。如果应用以对话为核心，使用语音问候也很合适。
下载音频
加载中表示内容正在加载。
下载音频
媒体静音（应用级）可选，由应用控制，用于关闭应用音频或媒体播放的声音；与系统控制的麦克风静音不同。
下载音频
取消媒体静音（应用级）可选，由应用控制，用于恢复应用音频或媒体播放的声音；与系统控制的麦克风取消静音不同。
下载音频
错误 / 公告表示发生了错误。
下载音频

应用不播放退出提示音；可以在退出时用语音总结刚结束的活动，退出反馈应仅限于这种形式。例如：“徒步结束。你走了 2.8 英里。”

自定义提示音

自定义提示音是应用独有、由应用自行设计的声音，不由系统提供。例如，带有品牌特征的应用启动音，或地图中的方向提示音。

避免：过度使用体验提示音

如果地图等体验会不时播放语音提示，且这些提示构成体验的核心，就应省去提示音，减少声音干扰。

关于如何制作自定义提示音，请阅读设计自定义提示音。
bodyEn:
Earcons, short for audio icons, provide brief audio cues or feedback to the user. Glasses provide earcons for common interactions.

Due to their cognitive load to learn, similar to visual icons, make sure to use earcons thoughtfully. Avoiding contradicting established sounds provided by the system.

  • Avoid earcons that need explanation that could be replaced by natural language phrase.
  • Avoid creating custom earcons that mimic system sounds, as they could confuse your users.
  • Users commonly learn earcons in context of an action.
  • Earcons should be simplified and intuitive.
  • Earcons are less descriptive compared to audio alerts.

Your app will pick up mobile earcons as well, so align the earcons used on glasses and your mobile app to keep the sound landscape consistent and simplified. For example, share the mute earcon between your app on a phone and glasses.

System earcons

Common system-wide sounds are provided by default and should be accounted for in your app. These can include:

Privacy and critical earcons

Critical hardware alerts and privacy earcons take priority over all audio. The microphone mute functions as a system-controlled privacy chime.

System sound Behavior
Microphone mute / unmute System-controlled privacy sound.
Critical Low Battery
  • Plays at a 20% minimum hardware volume floor
  • Bypasses DnD
  • Plays when disconnected from the phone
  • Completely suppresses all other audio streams, including active phone calls
Thermal Overheat Mitigation Triggered
Device Disconnected / Link Lost

Camera earcons

All camera and shutter earcons are non-mutable system sounds that play at a 60% minimum hardware volume floor and ignore Do Not Disturb (DnD) to protect wearer and bystander privacy.

When an app (such as a video-calling, or visual assistance app) requests access to open the user's front-facing camera stream, the system plays a non-mutable sequence that warns the user before the camera stream turns on and allows them to dismiss it if needed:

  1. Stream start sequence - Non-mutable earcon that warns the user an app is requesting access to open the front-facing camera stream.
  2. 3-second countdown - Audible 3-second countdown indicator before the camera stream turns on, giving the user time to dismiss or cancel camera access if needed.
  3. Stream on - Plays the non-mutable open-camera-stream earcon when the stream goes live.
  4. Stream off / dismiss - Unified non-mutable sound played when the camera stream turns off or when the user dismisses the countdown.

App earcons

Earcons can be found throughout apps, typically with the following functions. Consider including sounds for these, as they aren't provided by default:

Generic earcons

Generic earcons are standardized sounds, shared between apps to help users understand a common semantic sound language. You should use the provided sounds within your app.

Action Use Audio
App open An earcon to greet your user as your app opens. A verbal greeting is appropriate if your app is primarily conversational.
Download audio
Loading An earcon to indicate that content is loading.
Download audio
Media mute (App-level) Optional, app-controlled earcon for muting app audio or media playback (distinct from system-controlled microphone mute).
Download audio
Media unmute (App-level) Optional, app-controlled earcon for unmuting app audio or media playback (distinct from system-controlled microphone unmute).
Download audio
Error/Announcement An earcon to indicate that an error has occurred.
Download audio

Apps don't play exit earcons; keep exit signals limited to optional, spoken activity wrap-ups. For example, "Hike ended. You walked 2.8 miles."

Bespoke earcons

Bespoke earcons are customized sounds that are unique to your app, not provided by the system. For example, a branded app start or an orientation sound on Maps.

Don't

Over-use earcons for experiential alerts. If an experience, like Maps, has semi-frequent voice alerts which are core to the experience forego earcons to reduce auditory clutter.

For more information about creating bespoke earcons, read design custom sounds.

title: 语音提示
description: 用简洁、清楚的口语传达状态和下一步操作，并控制语音对体验的打扰。
body:
语音提示是以人声播报的信息。大多数语音提示应先播放一个提示音，让用户知道系统即将说话。由于两者通常配合使用，语音提示也应遵循音频焦点规则。

对于特殊交互或状态变化，例如连接丢失、结束翻译，语音提示能提供单靠提示音无法传达的明确说明。

如果用户在手机上进行的操作会影响眼镜体验，例如静音，就播放提示音，但省去语音提示。例如，用户在手机上将 Meet 通话静音。

避免：用语音打断体验

“通话已静音”这类可能打断当前体验的语音提示应少用，并尽量简短。

按需播报当前状态

如果应用已暂停，或者声音输出并不频繁，信息播报会在用户轻点眼镜时告知最新状态。这样用户不必回想应用刚才做了什么，也不会误以为应用已经停止。在无屏眼镜上，轻点触控板会触发状态播报，或控制播放与暂停。

译者注：原文另有“instead of holding Gemini or agents”，但未说明 holding 的含义。

通用语音提示

使用独特的声音并不会让通用语音提示获得额外益处；它们只为帮助用户理解音频应用的当前状态。它们使用默认的文字转语音方案。

在条件允许时，使用标准系统语音，保持一致，降低认知负担，也让体验更精致、周到。

以下是通用语音提示的几个例子：

自定义语音提示

这类声音具有独特性，也是音频体验的核心。允许对它们进行定制并融入品牌特征，对提升音频体验很重要。这类语音提示采用自定义文字转语音方案。

只在确有价值时使用品牌声音，例如体验中重要且明显的转折时刻。

怎样写好语音提示

设计和撰写应用的语音提示时，应考虑以下几点。

用日常语言，直接与用户交流

让应用的表达风格保持一致、简洁、口语化，并且真正有帮助。说明操作时，可以考虑用主动动词开头，清楚地引导用户。

例如，以“正在开始……”“正在关闭……”这样的主动表达说明动作。

建议：使用日常语言

使用用户熟悉、没有技术门槛的表达。

避免：为了简短而使用技术术语

即使为了缩短提示，也不要使用技术术语。

建议：直接对用户说话

用“你”这样的称呼，直接与用户交流。

避免：让系统成为叙述中心

不要让语音提示围绕系统自身展开，也不要用“我”或“我们”来表述。

兼顾简短与清楚

常见语音提示不应打断用户体验，因此，一条简短而有效的信息，优于准确到面面俱到却很冗长的说明。对于不常见的情况，多一点解释有助于避免认知过载，避免让用户自己猜解决办法。应考虑用户需要哪些信息，才能继续下一步。

考虑用户当时的环境

避免：默认用户只在使用眼镜

Voice alerts are vocal sound messages. Most voice alerts should be preceded with an earcon to let the user know the system is about to speak. Because they're typically accompanied by an earcon, voice alerts should also follow the audio focus patterns.

Use non-technical language.

Don't

Use technical terms, even for sake of brevity.

Speak to the user directly, with 'you' type language.

Don't

Write voice alerts to reference themselves, or use 'I' or 'We' wording.

Deliver only the information that's needed to proceed.

Don't

Get in the user's way with too much explanation or try to troubleshoot lengthy processes.

Do

Consider multidevice experiences. Call out when something happens on the phone versus wearable.

Don't

Assume the user is only using their glasses when creating voice alerts.

Voice alerts should follow standard UX writing methodology, especially with error messages.errors. Offer possible solutions by explaining why and how to resolve them. If a problem can be resolved with another attempt, encourage the user to do so. Don't write in a playful or mocking tone when an error occurs.

title: 音频焦点与多路声音
description: 根据内容的重要性，安排多路声音的混合、压低音量、暂停与优先级。
body:
无屏眼镜和带屏眼镜都通过同一组扬声器播放声音，由 Android 的音频焦点系统统一管理。应用开始播放时，会请求音频焦点。其他同时播放的音频会在后台平滑地降低音量、暂停或停止；这些调整不会额外播放提示音，也不会播报状态变化。了解无屏眼镜的音频与实体输入路由。

根据内容选择合适的处理方式

选择哪种方式，取决于用户错过一部分声音会损失什么。几秒钟的音乐被通知声盖过，不会丢失重要信息；但如果有声书里的一句话被盖过，用户就会错过情节。

  • 音乐和环境音：降低音量并继续播放，因为这样不会让用户错过信息。
  • 有声书等语音内容：暂停并回退播放位置，让用户不漏听信息。
  • 通话、实时翻译和智能体播报：需要用户集中注意力，因此其他可能打断它们的音频会暂停。
  • 简短而重要的更新，例如导航提示：遇到新传入的声音时，会短暂降低音量。
译者注：原文未说明这一步具体降低哪一路声音的音量。

系统会根据指定的内容类型分配处理方式。进一步了解音频焦点的优化方法。

提示音如何与其他声音同时播放

提示音与其他音频如何共存，取决于它承担的作用。用于确认用户自身操作的提示音即时且频繁，因此会直接叠加在正在播放的声音上。其他提示音携带用户需要听到的信息，会先短暂压低其他音频的音量，播放后再让其恢复。

针对不同处理方式设计提示音

  • 如果提示音采用混音叠加方式，它需要凭自身特征被听清：起音干净明确、时长紧凑、音色鲜明。其他声音不会主动让位，因此提示音本身必须有足够的辨识度。

  • 如果提示音会压低其他音频，设计时应考虑音量下降的曲线。其他声音降低音量需要一点时间；提示音应有清晰的起音，让用户在音量尚未降完时就能察觉。

系统优先级覆盖

隐私提示、通话和关键硬件警报等系统事件，始终优先于其他音频和应用音频焦点。这些事件也有相应的提示音与 LED 灯行为。
bodyEn:
Audio and display glasses route all sound through shared speakers, managed by Android's audio focus system. When an app starts playback, it requests audio focus. Concurrent streams seamlessly duck, pause, or stop in the background without playing audio cues or announcing state changes. Understand physical input routing for audio glasses.

Choose the behavior that fits your content

The right behavior depends on what the user would lose if they missed part of your audio. If a few seconds of music sit under a notification, nothing important is lost. If a sentence of an audiobook gets talked over, the user loses the story.

  • Music and ambient audio will duck and keep playing because there's no missed information.
  • Spoken content, like audiobooks, will pause and rewind the audio, so the user doesn't miss information.
  • Calls, live translation, and agent readouts need a user's full attention, so other audio interruptions are paused.
  • Short, important updates, like a navigation update, will duck briefly to the incoming sound.

The system assigns behavior based on the content type assigned. Learn more about optimizing audio focus.

Playing earcons alongside other audio

How an earcon plays over other audio depends on its job. Earcons that confirm the user's own action are instant and frequent, so they mix on top of whatever is playing. All other earcons carry information the user needs to hear, so they duck other audio briefly and then let it return.

Designing for each behavior

  • If your earcon mixes, design it to cut through on its own with a clean, defined attack, a tight duration and a distinct timbre. Nothing gets out of its way, so its character has to do the work.

  • If your earcon ducks, design it to account for the ducking curve. The other audio takes a moment to dip, so a clear start helps the earcon register before the dip finishes.

System Overrides

Certain system events—like privacy indicators, calls, and critical hardware alerts—always override other audio and app focus. They also have a set of earcon and LED behaviors.

title: 设计自定义提示音
description: 围绕听觉舒适、辨识度和硬件特性，为应用设计简洁一致的提示音。
body:
想为应用设计自己的提示音？本指南结合 Android 声音设计的最佳实践，介绍如何制作和引入自定义提示音。

每个提示音都应具备以下特征：

  • 即时、清晰：用户一听就能将它与背景环境声区分开。
  • 温和、克制：自然融入日常生活，避免惊吓和听觉疲劳。
  • 考虑数字信号处理：合理安排声音结构，避免经过设备内置放大器和限幅器处理后产生失真。

听觉舒适

听觉疲劳是可穿戴音频体验的主要问题。在录音棚监听音箱上听起来很轻柔的声音，如果每天在耳边重复 50 次，也可能令人烦躁。

  • 使用平滑的高架滤波器，衰减 8 kHz 以上的频率。贴近耳朵的尖锐瞬态声音容易迅速引起听觉疲劳。

  • 为音量调节等高频发生的交互，准备经过柔化和滤波处理的替代音效。

  • 如果提示音在很短的时间内反复触发，可以考虑抑制后续触发，或改为极简的轻点声，例如连续翻页时。

音频文件规格

交付音频文件时，优先选择轻量、高效的资源。以下参数有助于获得良好的音频质量。

参数规格
格式.ogg（Ogg Vorbis）
位深与采样率16 位 / 48 kHz（或 44.1 kHz）
资源大小上限小于 1 MB（未压缩）
峰值余量上限真实峰值为 −3.0 dB 至 −6.0 dB
声道格式立体声 / 双耳音频 / 单声道

顺应用户对声音的直觉

由于没有视觉提示，用户完全依赖听觉直觉来建立对操作系统的心智模型。设计应让用户的第一反应就是正确理解。利用已有的认知习惯，建立用户一听就能明白的声音语言。音高上行通常带有积极的意味：可以想象一段轻快上扬的大调音阶，将这类声音用于正向交互，有助于强化这种直觉。

类似地，音高下行会带来结束感，可以与负向、减少或关闭等操作搭配。

音高变化虽然有很强的表达力，但在传达关键状态变化时，如果仅依赖音高变化，就应格外谨慎，因为它们可能被嘈杂环境掩盖。可以将音高变化与节奏结合：例如，用两个快速上扬的铃音表示成功，用断续下行的脉冲表示警告。相关操作应保持一致的声音语言。

频谱设计

为了在不同声音环境中清楚传达信息，同时避免认知过载和身体不适，建议围绕以下三个主要频段安排提示音的频率分布：

频谱处理频率范围
温和的高通滤波100 Hz 以下
主要可听频段2 kHz–5 kHz
高架滤波衰减8 kHz 以上

将主要旋律和瞬态能量集中在主要可听频段。人耳对这一频段最敏感，因此无需提高总音量，提示音也能保持清楚可辨。

使用干脆的起音包络，让提示音能从交谈、交通或媒体播放的背景声中迅速被察觉。

使用有明确设计意图的合成波形，例如正弦波、干净的调频音色或清透的铃音。避免采用木头、纸张、弹指等自然声采样；这些材质感容易混入现实环境声，让用户产生混淆。

设备内置的数字信号处理会在播放时增加饱和失真。以干净、纯粹的基音作为起点，例如正弦波或低阶谐波，能确保在实际硬件上获得清晰、纯净的输出。

目标时长

眼镜用于日常生活场景，因此应保持声音环境简洁，避免噪声疲劳。设计交互声音时，要把外界环境声一并考虑进去。

类别目标时长示例特征
微交互15–60 ms短促、干脆。
操作确认80–220 ms稍长，起止清晰。
状态提醒250–500 ms更长，起止清晰。
重要体验时刻500–1000 ms更长，起止清晰。
bodyEn:
Interested in creating your own custom earcons for your app? This guide will help you create and introduce custom earcons with Android sound design best practices.

Every earcon should be:

  • Immediate & Legible: Instantly distinguishable from background environmental noise.
  • Acoustically Polite: Harmonious with everyday life, avoiding startle reflexes or ear fatigue.
  • DSP-Aware: Thoughtfully structured to prevent distortion when processed by onboard hardware amplifiers and limiters.

Ergonomics

Ear fatigue is the primary failure mode of wearable audio. What sounds subtle on studio monitors can become irritating after 50 daily repetitions near the ear.

  • Apply a smooth high-shelf filter to roll off frequencies above 8 kHz. Sharp near-ear transients cause rapid listener fatigue.

  • Provide softened, filtered alternate assets for high-frequency interactions. For example, volume.

  • If an earcon triggers repeatedly within a narrow window, consider suppressing secondary triggers or transition to a minimal click, like continuous paging.

Audio file support

When delivering audio files, lean and efficient assets work best. Here are some parameters to achieve a quality audio asset.

Parameter Specification
Format .ogg (Ogg Vorbis)
Bit Depth & Sample Rate 16-bit / 48 kHz (or 44.1 kHz)
Asset Size Limit < 1 MB (Uncompressed)
Headroom Ceilings -3.0 dB to -6.0 dB True Peak
Channel Format Stereo / Binaural / Mono

Mental models

Because there are no visual indicators, users rely entirely on auditory intuition to construct mental models of the operating system. The user should feel that the obvious answer is the right one. Use the existing mental model understanding to develop a language that the user will immediately recognize. Ascending pitch trajectories are often associated with positivity. Think of a happy major scale upward, these sounds can be paired with positive interactions to enforce such mental models.

Similarly, a descending trajectory evokes finality, which can pair with negative, decreasing, or dismissal actions.

While pitch trajectories are powerful, you should use caution when solely relying on them when conveying critical state changes as they can be lost in a noisy environment. Instead pitch motion and rhythmic patterning can be used. For example, success can be conveyed with two rapid ascending chimes or a warning can use a staccato descending pulse. Ensure related actions share sound language consistency.

Spectral design

To ensure clear communication in diverse auditory environments without causing cognitive overload or physical discomfort, we recommend aligning earcon frequency distribution across three primary spectral bands:

Spectral Region Frequency Range
Gentle High-Pass Filtering < 100 Hz
Target Audibility Band 2 kHz – 5 kHz
High-Shelf Roll-Off > 8 kHz

Concentrate the core melodic and transient energy in the target audibility band. The human ear exhibits peak sensitivity here, allowing cues to remain distinctly intelligible without raising the master volume.

Use crisp attack envelopes so cues register instantly through background chatter, traffic, or media playback.

Use synthetic, intentional waveforms (sine, clean FM, crystalline bells) rather than naturalistic or organic samples (wood, paper, snaps). Organic textures blend into real-world ambient sounds and create confusion.

Onboard DSP adds saturation during playback. Starting with clean, pure fundamentals (sine waves or low-order harmonics) ensures clean, pristine output on physical hardware.

Duration targets

Because the glasses are being used in everyday scenarios, it's important to keep the environment clean and avoid noise fatigue. Interactions need to be thought through with the background of ambient sound from the outside environment.

Category Target Duration Example
Micro-Interactions 15 ms—60 ms Short, crisp interactions.
Confirmations 80 ms—220 ms Slightly longer, with a clear beginning and end.
State Alerts 250 ms—500 ms Longer, with a clear beginning and end.
Hero Moments 500 ms — 1000 ms Longer, with a clear beginning and end.

text: 想为应用设计自己的提示音？本指南结合 Android 声音设计的最佳实践，介绍如何制作和引入自定义提示音。 每个提示音都应具备以下特征： 即时、清晰： 用户一听就能将它与背景环境声区分开。 温和、克制： 自然融入日常生活，避免惊吓和听觉疲劳。 考虑数字信号处理： 合理安排声音结构，避免经过设备内置放大器和限幅器处理后产生失真。 听觉舒适 听觉疲劳是可穿戴音频体验的主要问题。在录音棚监听音箱上听起来很轻柔的声音，如果每天在耳边重复 50 次，也可能令人烦躁。 使用平滑的高架滤波器，衰减 8 kHz 以上的频率。贴近耳朵的尖锐瞬态声音容易迅速引起听觉疲劳。 为音量调节等高频发生的交互，准备经过柔化和滤波处理的替代音效。 如果提示音在很短的时间内反复触发，可以考虑抑制后续触发，或改为极简的轻点声，例如连续翻页时。 音频文件规格 交付音频文件时，优先选择轻量、高效的资源。以下参数有助于获得良好的音频质量。 参数 规格 格式 .ogg（Ogg Vorbis） 位深与采样率 16 位 / 48 kHz（或 44.1 kHz） 资源大小上限 小于 1 MB（未压缩） 峰值余量上限 真实峰值为 −3.0 dB 至 −6.0 dB 声道格式 立体声 / 双耳音频 / 单声道 顺应用户对声音的直觉 由于没有视觉提示，用户完全依赖听觉直觉来建立对操作系统的心智模型。设计应让用户的第一反应就是正确理解。利用已有的认知习惯，建立用户一听就能明白的声音语言。音高上行通常带有积极的意味：可以想象一段轻快上扬的大调音阶，将这类声音用于正向交互，有助于强化这种直觉。 类似地，音高下行会带来结束感，可以与负向、减少或关闭等操作搭配。 音高变化虽然有很强的表达力，但在传达关键状态变化时，如果仅依赖音高变化，就应格外谨慎，因为它们可能被嘈杂环境掩盖。可以将音高变化与节奏结合：例如，用两个快速上扬的铃音表示成功，用断续下行的脉冲表示警告。相关操作应保持一致的声音语言。 频谱设计 为了在不同声音环境中清楚传达信息，同时避免认知过载和身体不适，建议围绕以下三个主要频段安排提示音的频率分布： 频谱处理 频率范围 温和的高通滤波 100 Hz 以下 主要可听频段 2 kHz–5 kHz 高架滤波衰减 8 kHz 以上 将主要旋律和瞬态能量集中在主要可听频段。人耳对这一频段最敏感，因此无需提高总音量，提示音也能保持清楚可辨。 使用干脆的起音包络，让提示音能从交谈、交通或媒体播放的背景声中迅速被察觉。 使用有明确设计意图的合成波形，例如正弦波、干净的调频音色或清透的铃音。避免采用木头、纸张、弹指等自然声采样；这些材质感容易混入现实环境声，让用户产生混淆。 设备内置的数字信号处理会在播放时增加饱和失真。以干净、纯粹的基音作为起点，例如正弦波或低阶谐波，能确保在实际硬件上获得清晰、纯净的输出。 目标时长 眼镜用于日常生活场景，因此应保持声音环境简洁，避免噪声疲劳。设计交互声音时，要把外界环境声一并考虑进去。 类别 目标时长 示例特征 微交互 15–60 ms 短促、干脆。 操作确认 80–220 ms 稍长，起止清晰。 状态提醒 250–500 ms 更长，起止清晰。 重要体验时刻 500–1000 ms 更长，起止清晰。

title: 视觉样式
description: 以清晰、易读、低干扰为目标，使用适合眼镜显示的颜色、字体和形状。
body:
让界面清晰、易读，尽量减少干扰。

带屏眼镜的近眼显示区域很小，视觉设计需要围绕这一限制展开：强调清晰、易读和低干扰，同时牢记用户的主要注意力仍在现实世界。视觉元素应轮廓清楚、对比鲜明，只在有需要时出现，在不再相关时迅速淡出。

Jetpack Compose Glimmer 采用精简的主题体系，让内容在眼镜上清楚可见。可以定制颜色和字体，以传达不同含义，并保持应用自身的视觉一致性。

建议：使用圆角

使用圆角，避免组件的角部吸走用户的注意力。

避免：过度定制尖锐形状

尖锐转角容易形成吸引视线停留的局部区域；在沉浸式和增强现实体验中，这种影响更加明显。
bodyEn:
Design for clarity, legibility, and minimal distraction.

Visual design principles emphasize clarity, legibility, and minimal distraction, adapted to the unique constraints of a small, near-eye display on display glasses. Consider the limited display area and the user's primary focus on the real world. Visual elements should be designed to be crisp, high-contrast, and appear only when necessary, quickly fading when no longer relevant.

Jetpack Compose Glimmer's design language features a simplified theme for optimal visibility on glasses. Color and type can be customized for semantic expression and app cohesion.

Do

Embrace rounded corners to avoid drawing the user's attention into component corners.

Don't

Overly customize shape with sharp corners, they can create visual pockets that lead the user's eye into, which on immersive and augmented experiences have greater affect.

title: 色彩
description: 结合透视显示、现实背景和功耗，建立清晰克制的配色体系。
body:
眼镜上的用色，需要同时考虑显示特性、环境和用户认知。配色经过精细调整，以适应加色式显示，并让观看更舒适。应克制地使用颜色，让界面与现实环境协调；颜色可以用来强调重要操作、呈现图像，或传达具体含义。

在光学透视显示中，黑色呈现为透明。设计时要记住：深色会显得暗淡或透明；也可以利用这一特性营造深度感。

配色体系

眼镜的配色体系是一组用于定义应用主题的颜色令牌或颜色角色，由 3 种强调色角色、6 种界面底板色（或中性色）角色，以及各自对应的前景色角色组成。这里的颜色角色与手机端相似，使用方式也应保持一致。

强调色也可以用于前景内容，但应限于少量强调。

建议：以白色文字为主

大多数文字内容使用白色，需要强调的文字可以使用其他颜色。

避免：所有文字都使用彩色

不要给全部文字内容着色。

提示：Jetpack Compose Glimmer Figma 套件包含颜色示意表，可以查看并定制各颜色角色及其数值。

定制颜色

为眼镜定制颜色时，关键是尽量减少视觉遮挡，并与现实环境协调。应优先保证内容在不同光照下都能读清。仔细平衡亮度与饱和度，让颜色能被迅速辨认。

主色可以使用品牌色或主要交互色。选择时，需要考虑对比度、饱和度以及功耗。

提示：可以参考 Jetpack Compose Glimmer Skill，辅助计算对比度指标。

优化品牌色与语义色

用于表达品牌、操作或系统警报的颜色，必须满足以下要求：

  • 足够亮，保证内容可读。
  • 具有足够的饱和度，使其呈现出可辨识的色彩。
  • 在 HCT 色彩空间中，前景与背景的明度（Tone）差至少为 66%。
译者注：本页原文分别使用“66%”“明度差 70（7:1）”和“约 66”，表述不一致；这里保留各处原值。

进一步了解 Jetpack Compose Glimmer 主题。

功耗

不同颜色的功耗和发热不同。如下图所示，在明度相同的条件下比较，绿色最省电，蓝色耗电最多。应尽量减少被点亮的像素数量。屏幕越亮，显示部件就越热；不要让全屏显示纯白，否则可能触发过热保护。

建议：检查各种背景下的对比度

考虑用户可能遇到的所有背景，检查界面与背景之间的对比度。

避免：界面在不同背景上对比不足

对比度不足可能造成视觉疲劳，让内容难以辨读。

为了在各种背景上保持足够对比，原文要求前景与背景颜色的明度差达到“70（7:1）”。可以将设计稿设为 Screen（滤色）混合模式进行检查。

建议：使用较低饱和度的颜色

使用较低饱和度的颜色。

避免：颜色过度饱和

过度饱和的颜色可能无法正确显示，并影响可读性。

应避免自行定制界面底板。

深色容器

容器通常必须把注意力留给其中的内容，避免自身形成干扰：

  • 为了获得最高对比度，界面底板必须使用黑色。
  • 处于焦点状态时，底板明度不应高于 34%，以保证前景元素清楚可读。
  • 描边应看得见，但保持克制。

建议：深色底板，明亮内容

使用深色界面底板和明亮的前景内容。

避免：明亮或填色的底板

不要使用明亮或填色的界面底板。

建议：拉开底板与文字的明度

让底板与文字之间有足够对比；原文建议检查两者的明度差是否约为 66。

避免：底板与文字太接近

不要让底板和文字的明度过于接近，导致对比不足。

建议：让不同底板角色形成层次

确保 Surface 与 Surface Variants 之间有足够的明度差，以建立必要的视觉层次。

避免：不同底板角色明度过近

不要让 Surface 与其变体的明度过于接近；原文在此标注了“约 20 的差值”。

译者注：原文未说明“约 20”是建议差值还是反例数值。

可以定制描边，为界面加入品牌特征或更有表现力的视觉语言。

建议：使用默认颜色

默认颜色已针对眼镜显示进行了充分优化。

避免：同时使用多种描边色

不要让描边混用多种颜色。

注意：协调不同状态的描边颜色

定制颜色时，谨慎处理焦点状态与默认状态的描边，使两者保持协调。

建议：所有交互状态都有足够对比

确保界面在每种交互状态下都保持足够的对比度。

避免：交互状态对比度过低

不要把交互状态的对比度降得过低。
bodyEn:
Color considers display, environment, and cognition. Color on glasses uses a highly-refined palette to support the behavior of additive displays and to optimize for visual comfort. The use of color on glasses should be used judiciously to harmonize with the real world, to indicate important actions, display imagery or provide semantic meaning.

Black is transparent on optical-see-through display. Keep this in mind when designing as darker color will appear dull or transparent, but this can also be used to create depth.

Color scheme

The glasses color scheme (collection of color tokens or roles to theme the color of your app) consists of 3 accent roles, 6 surface (or neutral roles), and their on-color counterparts. The color roles are similar to their mobile scheme roles and should be used in the same manner.

Accent colors can be used for on color as limited emphasis.

Do

Use white text for most of your text content. Font color can be used for emphasized text.

Don't

Use color text for all content.
Note: The Jetpack Compose Glimmer Figma kit includes a color schematic with roles and values to customize.

Customize color

When customizing colors for glasses, minimal visual obstruction and harmonization with the real world is crucial, prioritize legibility across varying lighting conditions. Carefully calibrate colors to balance brightness against saturation to be instantly discernible.

Primary color can be customized to use your brand or primary interaction color. Consider the contrast, saturation, and power usage of the chosen color.

Note: Try out the Jetpack Compose Glimmer Skill for help with contrast calculation metrics.

Optimized brand and semantic colors

Colors that represent brand, actions, or system alerts must be:

  • Bright enough to be legible
  • Saturated enough to be discernible as a color
  • Ensure at least a 66% tone difference between foreground and background using the HCT color space.

Learn more on Jetpack Compose Glimmer theme.

Power usage

Some colors use more power and generate more heat than others. Green is the least power hungry, blue is the most, when comparing colors of equal tone as seen on the right. Minimize the number of pixels you light up. The brighter the screen, the hotter the display gets. Don't fill the screen with all white, as this can cause thermal mitigation.

Do

Take into account contrast between all backgrounds your users will encounter.

Don't

Have too little contrast for UI elements on various backgrounds, this can create eyestrain and illegibility.
In order to have enough contrast over every background you need to have a contrast difference of 70 (7:1) in the tone of the foreground and background colors. You can test this out by setting your designs to screen blend mode.

Do

Use desaturated colors.

Don't

Use overly saturated colors. They may not display properly and disrupt legibility.

Customized surfaces should be avoided.

Dark container colors

Containers generally must focus on displaying content that is within them, without being distracting:

  • Surfaces must be black for highest contrast.
  • Surfaces should be no lighter than 34% tone in their focused state to maintain legibility for foreground elements.
  • Outlines should be visible but subtle.

Do

Use dark surfaces and bright content.

Don't

Use bright or filled surfaces.

Do

Provide contrast between surface and text. Approximate 66 tone difference is suggested to check for.

Don't

Allow surface and text contrast to be too close.

Do

Make sure Surface and Surface Variants have enough tone difference to create the necessary visual hierarchy.

Don't

Make Surface and Surface variant too close in tone (around 20 difference).

Outline customization is possible to add branding or expressive UI.

Do

Use the default colors. These have been highly optimized for glasses display.

Don't

Use multiple outline colors.

Warning

Be careful and harmonize custom colors between focus and default state outlines.

Customizing the outline focus with blue: the focus state highlight is made of 2 outlines, color is applied to layer 2 to tint the focus state.

Do

Make sure there is enough contrast across all interaction states.

Don't

Change the contrast on interaction states to minimal contrast.
